From the README's limitations section, in descending order of importance: lexical groundedness is a citation-hygiene proxy that paraphrase can defeat, not entailment; the gate's paired tests and intervals treat the {{ds.n_cases}} cases as a sample of questions but say nothing about run-to-run model noise, which needs repeated runs; the demo SUT is a deterministic stand-in, so committed latency and token figures characterize the harness, not an LLM; token counts are heuristic and labelled as such; abstention is a measured open gap requiring semantic matching ({{v2.n_abstained}} of {{v2.n_abstention_correct}} unanswerable questions refused by v2); retrieval ground truth is hand-declared for a {{ds.n_docs}}-document corpus and does not scale as-is; and the sync runner's thread-based timeout bounds its wait but cannot kill a hung call in Python (the async runner cancels it). Each limitation is documented where the relevant code lives rather than in a disclaimer nobody reads.
